upstream: LingBot-Depth v0.5 (MDM v2, DINOv2 ViT-L/14 RGB-D)
task: RGB-D depth refinement: noisy/holey sensor depth + aligned RGB -> hole-filled metric depth + trust mask

licence.detail: Apache-2.0 on both the code repo and the published weights (declared on the model card, no gated agreement). The DINOv2 backbone is Apache-2.0 for code and weights as well, and the training data is first-party — so no part of the chain is encumbered.

toolchain.note: Recorded so a future failure can be attributed. The host HBDK and the board HBRT must match; 3.7.0 host pairs with 4.0.5 board.

graph_rewrite.what: Token preparation rebuilt without depth_masking, which drops depth tokens whose 14x14 patch holds no valid reading and therefore makes the sequence length data-dependent.

fidelity_vs_upstream.note: Bit-identical to upstream's own forward when the RGB resize antialiases. The rewrite itself introduces nothing.

cost_of_dropping_the_masking.caveat: Measured on scenes that are 87-100% valid depth. Sparse input (lidar, sparse feature depths) is NOT covered by this number, and is the case where the dropped tokens carry information.

host_preprocessing.note: The .hbm holds only static tensor ops; resize, normalisation and the log remap are the host's job. calib.py is the single definition, BCDL's src/tasks/depth_refine.cc mirrors it.

measured.note: Measured on S100P through BCDL's own Engine, so the figures include the packed -> padded-stride input scatter the runtime performs. Board was verified quiet first via a known model's latency, not by load average.

node_info.note: The int8 build's per-layer report is the interesting one -- see rejected_builds. For the int16 build the end-to-end figures above are the gate.

performance_analysis.attention_matmul: 4.3 ms of compute inside a 21.9 ms slot
performance_analysis.cause: Image and depth tokens are concatenated, so the attention sequence is 1 + 2N. At N=1200 that is 2401, and a 16 x 2401 x 2401 int16 score matrix is 184 MB, materialised to DDR twice per block across 24 blocks.
performance_analysis.hbdk_estimate_note: 2.1x optimistic against 1457 ms measured, while the same estimator was within 9% on the int8 build (235 vs 255 ms). Do not trust the compiler's latency estimate on a DDR-bound graph.

per_block_cost_from_probes.note: int8 probes via --fast-perf. Extrapolating to 24 blocks predicted 220 ms against 255 ms measured -- a cheap way to size a transformer before paying for a full compile.

token_budget.note: The only real latency lever, and quadratic. fp32 accuracy measured against a 3600-token reference on the bundled scenes. Every row here costs less than the 2.92% int16 quantisation already costs, so drop tokens before reaching for anything cleverer.
token_budget.why_1200: Bottom of upstream's trained range [1200, 3600], and its decoder pyramid lands exactly on 480x640 (30x40 x16), making the graph's final resize the identity.

rejected_builds.name: int8 (all)
rejected_builds.why: Not noise -- the dynamic range collapses, against a float range of 0.97-45.8 m. Compiles without a single warning. A 24-layer ViT-L is the case the all-int16 rule exists for.

predicted_in_advance.source: *_quant_info.json per-layer cosine, read before spending board time
predicted_in_advance.worst_nodes: LayerNorm and softmax Mul at 0.006 cosine
predicted_in_advance.how_to_read_it: Per-layer cosine is normally a localisation tool rather than a gate -- LAS2 ships with two thirds of layers below 0.99 and a 0.99995 output. What is diagnostic here is a whole OPERATOR CLASS collapsing to ~0, not a broad mild sag. Group the report by op type before judging.

recipe_fidelity.what: This recipe's calib.py was re-run against the upstream example scenes and its output compared against the calibration set the shipped .hbm was actually built from.
recipe_fidelity.result: bit-identical, max abs difference 0.0 across all 15 pairs of both inputs
recipe_fidelity.why_it_matters: The recipe is executable rather than reconstructed from notes: the preprocessing here IS the preprocessing the shipped model was calibrated with, not a description of it.

calibration.source: the eight scenes bundled with the upstream repo, plus horizontal mirrors, one scene held out as the golden
calibration.caveat: Domain-matched to upstream's examples, not to any particular camera. Deploying against a specific depth source (a stereo rig through LAS2, a given ToF module) warrants recalibrating on that source -- a ten-minute job, and this repo's own LAS2 and PIDNet results show domain match beating sample count.

runtime_integration.note: BCDL's tasks/depth_refine drives this model end to end: hole-filling, scale consistency against the input depth, point-cloud geometry, and C++/numpy preprocessing parity all asserted on-board (tests/test_depth_refine_board_py.py).
